land.text: Harsha's realm, 606-647 on the Kannauj page, from which Yashovarman seized power after Harsha died without an heir

predecessors.note: The Kannauj page gives no date for Yashovarman's seizure and the Yashovarman page names Arunasva as his predecessor; Cliopatria's Harsha's Empire ends in 655, so a gap of about seventy years lies between the rows.

successors.note: 816: Nagabhata II 'invaded Kannauj, defeated Chakrayudha, and then made Kannauj his capital' (Ayudha page).

capitals.name: Kannauj (Kanyakubja)
capitals.note: Yashovarman page infobox: capital Kannauj, then called Kanyakubja. Coordinates 27 04 N 79 55 E from the Kannauj page infobox. The Kannauj page calls it the 'capital city of the Panchala Kingdom' under Vajrayudha and capital of the Ayudhas.

correction.text: the 732 shape held for the seven years before it; the page gives Yashovarman's conquests (Bihar, Bengal and beyond) only through the Gaudavaho and gives no year for them

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Yashovarman page infobox gives his reign as 725-752 (Tripathi's calculation; Smith proposed c. 728-745), but Cliopatria's Kannauj-Varman row begins in 732. Neither the Kannauj nor the Yashovarman page gives an area, so the shape's area cannot be compared.

0.559 M km2 for 732-740. By the gazetteer the shape holds all of the Doab and Awadh, 95% of Haryana, 96% of Magadha, 64% of Bihar, 29% of Punjab, 15% of Rajasthan, 5% of Nepal and 4% of Kashmir. The Yashovarman page's only evidence of reach is the Gaudavaho (conquests of Bihar, Bengal, the western Deccan, the Indus valley and Kashmir, which Tripathi calls 'more like fiction than sober history'), a temple at Harischandranagari (Ayodhya), an inscription at Nalanda and coins; Majumdar calls him 'unquestionably the most powerful king' of the region. The core is supported, the Punjab and Haryana parts are unverified. Neither the Kannauj nor the Yashovarman page gives an area, so the shape's area cannot be compared.

0.573 M km2 for 741-750. The alliance with Lalitaditya broke c. 740 and Kalhana has Yashovarman 'submitted to him after a long war and offered a peace treaty'; Mishra has him acknowledge Lalitaditya's suzerainty 'for a short period' and become practically independent later; Tripathi argues for a 'nominal acknowledgement of supremacy' with Yashovarman staying on the throne. The page does not say Lalitaditya annexed Kannauj, and Cliopatria keeps the shape unchanged, so the war is a short contest (ledger) and the shape stands. Neither the Kannauj nor the Yashovarman page gives an area, so the shape's area cannot be compared.

0.570 M km2 for 751-767. Yashovarman's reign ends 752 on the infobox; Jain chronicles give his son Ama 749-753. The page says nothing about the kingdom's extent afterwards, but says the successors 'were all weak rulers' (Ayudha page), so the shape is unverified and probably generous. Neither the Kannauj nor the Yashovarman page gives an area, so the shape's area cannot be compared.

0.570 M km2 for 768-771, identical to 751. The Ayudha page: 'Vajrayudha, who ascended to the throne in 770 CE, was the first ruler of the dynasty' and 'deposed the Varmans'; the Varman row therefore ends in 770, a year before Cliopatria's 771, and the Ayudha kingdom continues the same state (ledger: rename 770). The shape is kept to 771 and the 771 loss narrows it for the following years.

correction.text: Kannauj and the Doab: the Ayudha kingdom from Kannauj whose end in 816 was the invasion of the Doab; extent beyond that is on no page opened

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 772-815, a period Cliopatria's Kannauj row lacks (its Pratihara shape of 772-777 holds half of Kannauj, which the Pratihara dossier removes). The Ayudha page gives the dynasty 'c. 770' to 'c. 816', ruling from Kannauj, with no territory; the Tripartite Struggle page shows the contest for 'the throne of Kannauj' and the Doab as its field, ending when Nagabhata II 'invaded the Doab' in 816. The shape is therefore the Doab and a 150 km circle round Kannauj, a minimal reading; the Varman periphery (Haryana, Awadh, Magadha) is on no page.

region.text: Kannauj, then called Kanyakubja, and the Doab round it

ledger.note: 725: Yashovarman founds the Varman dynasty at Kannauj (Kanyakubja). The Yashovarman page infobox gives his reign 725-752 (Tripathi's calculation) and calls him the 'first king of the Varman dynasty'; Smith proposed c. 728-745, so the year is one scholar's. Origin disputed (an incarnation of Vishnu or a kshatriya of the Lunar dynasty in the Gaudavaho; Cunningham suggested a Maukhari link). The page names Kannauj, not a boundary.

c. 740: the Kashmiri alliance breaks and Lalitaditya attacks Kannauj. The Yashovarman page: the alliance with Muktapida, with whom he had defeated the Tibetans, collapsed around 740; Majumdar says Lalitaditya defeated him and annexed his lands, Tripathi that he may have stayed on the throne after a nominal acknowledgement of supremacy. The Lalitaditya page dates the invasion 14 August 733 (Jacobi), sometime before 736 (Stein), 730 or earlier (Goetz) and after 736 (Mishra); Kalhana gives no year. The year here is the Yashovarman page's.

c. 741: the war ends with Yashovarman still reigning. The Lalitaditya page: Kalhana has him submit 'after a long war and offered a peace treaty', Mishra that he acknowledged Lalitaditya's suzerainty 'for a short period' and became practically independent later; no year for the end. The end year is bridging: Cliopatria keeps the Kannauj shape unchanged and the page does not say Kanyakubja was held by Kashmir afterwards (Kalhana: it 'came under Lalitaditya's control'). The Karkota dossier may record the suzerainty as a vassal relation.

770: Vajrayudha deposes the Varmans and the Ayudha dynasty rules Kannauj. 'Vajrayudha, who ascended to the throne in 770 CE, was the first ruler of the dynasty'; 'The dynasty was established when Vajrayudha deposed the Varmans and started ruling over Kannauj.' Infobox 'Established: c. 770', preceded by the Varman dynasty. Same state and colour (rule 2).

region.text: the periphery of Cliopatria's Varman shape outside the Kannauj core and the Doab

ledger.note: 771: the Varman realm is reduced to the Kannauj core. The Ayudha page says Yashovarman's successors 'were all weak rulers who did not demonstrate the skills to run and defend the kingdom' but names no land lost; the pages opened give the Ayudha kingdom no territory beyond Kannauj and the Doab. Bridging from the pages' silence: the periphery of Cliopatria's 768 shape (Haryana, Awadh, Magadha, Bihar, Punjab) is dropped, and no taker is named.

c. 786: Dhruva of the Rashtrakutas marches on Kannauj. The Tripartite Struggle page has Dhruva defeat Vatsaraja and then Dharmapala in the Doab, only meant to raid, not conquer; the Pratihara page dates his crossing of the Narmada and attempt on Kannauj c. 786 (see the gurjara-pratihara-dynasty dossier). This page gives no year for the start.
790: Dhruva goes home. 'He thus returned to the South in 790.' Kannauj is then taken by Dharmapala (c. 791), who installs Chakrayudha as a vassal; that relation belongs to the Pala dossier.

816: Nagabhata II takes Kannauj. 'In 816, Nagabhata II invaded the Doab, and defeated king Chakrayudha and proclaimed himself the King of Kannauj.' The Ayudha page: he 'invaded Kannauj, defeated Chakrayudha, and then made Kannauj his capital'. Dharmapala's later defeat at Monghyr is undated.
816: the Ayudhas end. 'This marked the end of the Ayudhas.' (Infobox 'Disestablished: c. 816'.) Kannauj becomes the Pratihara capital.

wars.name: Yashovarman and Lalitaditya's alliance against the Tibetans
wars.outcome: The Yashovarman page says he was briefly allied with Muktapida and the two defeated the Tibetans; no land is said to have changed hands.
wars.note: Undated on the page; bracketed by Yashovarman's accession (725 on the infobox) and the collapse of the alliance around 740. The page adds that he sent a minister to China in 731, which Majumdar reads as a diplomatic tie with the Tang.

wars.name: War of Lalitaditya and Yashovarman
wars.outcome: Kalhana: Yashovarman submitted after a long war and was then uprooted; modern historians differ on whether Kannauj was annexed (Majumdar) or Yashovarman stayed on his throne after a nominal acknowledgement of supremacy (Tripathi, Mishra).
wars.note: Dates range from 730 or earlier (Goetz) and 14 August 733 (Jacobi) to after 736 and before Yashovarman's death in 749-753 (Mishra); the ledger uses c. 740 from the Yashovarman page.

wars.name: Tripartite Struggle
wars.outcome: Pratihara victory in 816: Nagabhata II defeats Chakrayudha, Dharmapala's nominee, and proclaims himself king of Kannauj; the Ayudha dynasty ends.
wars.note: Dhruva raids to 790; Dharmapala installs Chakrayudha c. 791; Govinda III takes the submission of Dharmapala and Chakrayudha (793-814, undated).

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is on any page; the extent of the kingdom is a poem's claim (Gaudavaho) before 770 and a minimal Kannauj-and-Doab reading after.

sources.note: Identity, reign 725-752, Varman dynasty, Gaudavaho conquests, the break with Lalitaditya c. 740, Ama.

sources.title: Lalitaditya Muktapida

sources.title: Ayudha dynasty
sources.note: c. 770 to c. 816, Vajrayudha, Indrayudha 783, Chakrayudha, the end in 816.

sources.note: 785-816: Dhruva, Dharmapala c. 791, Govinda III, Nagabhata II in 816.

notes: Scope decision: Cliopatria's Kannauj-Varman row ends in 771, but the Ayudha page has the Ayudhas succeed the Varmans at Kannauj in 770 by deposition and hold the city until Nagabhata II took it in 816, so the dossier keeps one Kannauj state to 816 with a rename event (rule 2). If the orchestrator prefers the Cliopatria life 732..771, cut the 772-815 keyframe and the 771-816 events; the 816 gain and the vassal tint in gurjara-pratihara-dynasty then stand alone. The 772-815 shape (Kannauj and the Doab) and the 771 loss are minimal readings from the pages' silence (confidence 1): no page opened gives the Ayudha kingdom's land, the taker of the Varman periphery (Pala in Bihar and Magadha, Karkota in the north-west are the candidates), or Yashovarman's real extent. Pala suzerainty over Kannauj from c. 791 (Dharmapala installs Chakrayudha) and the Karkota suzerainty after c. 740 are the suzerains' vassal events; they are not duplicated here. Not read within the budget of five pages: the Karkota dynasty, Harsha, Pala and Maukhari articles, the Gaudavaho, and Seshat. The Lalitaditya page does not mention the Ayudhas and the Ayudha page does not mention Lalitaditya: it names Jayapida as the probable conqueror of Vajrayudha, which the page ties to no date. Rulers are not listed: the pages give Yashovarman 725-752 (infobox; Smith c. 728-745), Ama 749-753 (Jain chronicles, overlapping), Vajrayudha 770-783 and Chakrayudha c. 791-816 with Indrayudha's end undated and the Varman rulers between 753 and 770 unnamed. Gazetteer: nothing unknown; 'Doab' and 'Awadh' resolve.
